title: ICE Is Inspiring Latinos to Vote in Historic Numbers
gist: Contrary to fears that ICE surges would suppress turnout, Latino early voting in the 2026 midterms is surging. By October 27, 3.8 million Hispanic and Latino voters had cast ballots nationwide, up from 2.35 million by the same date in 2022. In Texas, half of the more than 400,000 early voters who skipped 2024 are Latino. Organizers attribute the surge to anti-ICE defiance.

themes.theme: Early-vote data shows a Latino surge

insights.so_what: A roughly 60 percent jump in Latino early voting could shift close races and congressional control.
